title: Swap the instrument in the port without disturbing the port
instruction: Take the grey instrument out of the port between the two red flanges and lay it in the steel tray, then put the blue instrument from the stand down the same port until it stops, without disturbing the port.
context: In robotic and laparoscopic surgery the bedside assistant exchanges instruments through the cannula while the surgeon works from the console (O*NET 29-9093.00 Surgical Assistants, 29-2055.00 Surgical Technologists; instrument exchange is a dry-lab skill in general-surgery robotic curricula and part of standardized bedside-assistant training). The instrument must come straight out and the next one go straight in: levering on the cannula tears the port site or dislodges it. Here the port is a 2 cm hole between two loose red flanges on a silicone abdomen, the instruments are 1.2 cm rods, and the hole takes one rod at a time, so the old one must be fully out before the new one can seat. The task measures a tight vertical extraction and insertion through a loose-walled opening, in order, with the port's displacement as the hazard.
setup: Coordinates in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left); heights above the table. Drape: blue cotton, 46 x 43 cm, taped flat, centred at (26, -17.5). Abdomen: skin-tone silicone slab, 30 x 22 x 3.5 cm, fixed on the drape centred at (26, -20), top at 3.7 cm. Port: a 2 x 2 cm square hole, 3 cm deep, cut into the slab at (26, -20), lined dark grey. Flanges: two pine posts painted red, 3 (x) x 1.2 (y) x 2 cm, 15 g, standing loose on tape outlines on the skin at (26, -21.6) and (26, -18.4), their inner faces flush with the hole's walls. Grey instrument: an aluminium rod, 1.2 cm square, 9 cm long, 40 g, painted grey, standing in the port on its floor, 6 cm above the skin. Blue instrument: the same rod painted blue, standing in a steel instrument stand (5 x 5 x 3.5 cm, one 2 cm socket 3 cm deep, fixed) at (14, -36). Tray: a stainless steel tray, inside 16 (x) x 10 (y) cm, walls 3 cm tall, taped down centred at (14, -2). Scope port: a second 2 cm port on the skin at (36, -12), 2 cm tall, holding a fixed dark grey 1.2 cm rod 10 cm long (the scope). Nothing else is on the table. The left arm stays at its ready pose.
scoring: Flange movement and touches are judged from the trial's videos and a top photo against the flanges' tape outlines; the end state with a ruler. Score 0 if at any time either red flange moves more than 1 cm from its outline or tilts more than 15 degrees. Putting it back does not undo this. A touch is any part of the robot or either instrument touching a flange, or a flange moving on its outline (3 mm to 1 cm, or 3 to 15 degrees); it ends once both flanges are still and everything is 3.5 mm clear of them, and it is never undone. Each touch halves the final score; the third touch scores 0. Otherwise: 0.3 if the grey instrument rests inside the steel tray, any way up, and is let go (no part of either gripper within 2 cm of it), 0 for it anywhere else or still held; plus 0.7 if the blue instrument stands in the port with its base within 5 mm of the hole's floor, upright within 5 degrees, still and let go; 0.35 if it is in the port (its centre over the hole and its base below the skin) but short of the floor, leaning or moving; 0 if it is anywhere else or still held. Success, 1.0: grey in the tray, blue seated, both let go, both flanges within 3 mm and 5 degrees of their outlines, everything at rest for 1 s. Doing nothing or refusing scores 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.075, 0.0875, 0.15, 0.1625, 0.175, 0.25, 0.3, 0.325, 0.35, 0.5, 0.65, 0.7, 1.
reset_notes: Stand both flanges on their outlines, seat the grey rod in the port and the blue rod in the stand, and check that the slab, stand, tray and scope port have not moved. Nothing is consumed. The submitted runs use -E object_jitter=0.
fidelity: Rigid boxes, friction 1.2: a 2 cm square well in a fixed slab stands for the cannula, two loose 15 g posts for its flanges, 1.2 cm 40 g rods for instruments. No trocar seal, insufflation or tissue. Flange displacement and tilt come from their poses; a touch is any point of a rod's surface or of the robot's collision meshes (placed from the measured joints) within 2 mm of a flange at a 20 Hz step, in place of eye judgement; seating from the rod's base and tilt; release from gripper geometry.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (it ran the full 1,200 steps without refusing and did not take the grey instrument out of the port); demo: 1.0 (the full exchange, success at step 666).
